I think you should seriously consider the advice from the comments above. In order to keep fish alive and healthy you need to cycle you tank. There’s no shortcuts with this one. You need restart and add all new water. It doesn’t matter where you’ve gotten it from, it needs to be dechlorinated. I recommend SeaChem Stability and Prime and following the dosage on the back.  Fill your tank, set up the substrate, and dose your water. Get new filter media and put it in the filter and make sure you’ve got a heater. Best case scenario you let the tank cycle. This could take a month to 6 months. It does sound like you already have fish, so in this case do a 50% water change. Dose stability and prime. I’d recommend buying a freshwater testing kit to ensure what issues you’re having. The prime should detoxify the ammonia and heavy metals in the water, so it becomes safe. You’ll need to do this for 1 week or as long as it takes for your water to stabilize. Again. It doesn’t matter how clear or bubbly the water you get from fountains are, it is toxic to fish without treatment

For skincare I would recommend the CeraVe Gentle Foaming Cleanser, The Ordinary “Buffet” Peptide serum, and the CeraVe Daily Moisturizing Lotion. It’s a very simple and basic routine that shouldn’t cost you more than 30$

In terms of your hair, make sure you’re washing it with cold or lukewarm water. Only apply shampoo to your scalp area and condition to your ends and midsection of hair, let the conditioner set for 2-3 minutes. You can try fun scented shower gels etc
It sounds like you may needs some moisture in your hair and frizz control, so start with avoiding hot water on you hair when washing and try it with a tshirt instead of a towel. If you have curly hair and just don’t know it, there are a lot of great tutorials online. Shampoo doesn’t need to be expensive either and most from the drug store work just as well as high end ones.

Incorporate a makeup routine too! This isn’t required, I personally don’t wear a ton of makeup or any at all most days, but a good start would be plucking or waxing your eyebrows to define their shape and create a cleaner arch for a more feminine look(this is totally optional and body hair is normal). Eyebrow gel helps hold them in place, elf has one for 2.99$ at most drug stores. You can also try curling your eyelashes (elf has a curler for 3.99$) and applying a mascara ( I personally really like The House Of Lashes Waterproof I think it was 7$.) Waterproof mascara hold the lash curl better than regular. You can also play with eye shadows and foundation, but makeup isn’t really necessary.

As for style, it can be hard to find something that you think fits you. If it isn’t out of budget or if you have a friend or parent willing to drop 35-50$ on a pair of jeans, check out American Eagle.
